# C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management

*Level 1 card. 5 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from thread/task misuse, synchronization overhead, contention, or failure to exploit available parallelism. This includes heavyweight or over-broad locking (excessive contention), architectural bottlenecks that force serial execution (serial bottleneck), threads or tasks that are never properly stopped (leaked threads), running heavy work on the main/UI thread (blocking main thread), and executing independent work serially when concurrency would reduce total time and energy (missed parallelism). In Python, the GIL makes threading ineffective for CPU-bound work; use multiprocessing for CPU-bound and asyncio/threading for I/O-bound tasks.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | narrow the critical section to the state that actually needs protecting | yes, scales with input |
| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | replicate or pool the bottleneck resource | yes, scales with input |
| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | give the worker a shutdown path, or make it a daemon | **no — advisory only** |
| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | move the blocking work off the loop | yes, scales with call count |
| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | run the independent items concurrently, matching the pool to the workload | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C11.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S5.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from an already-open category is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because a static signal pointed at it, not because a smell is there.
